basis: Inherited susceptibility to a lymphoid blood-cell neoplasm; susceptibility alone does not establish active lymphoma or immune dysfunction.
Vitreoretinal degeneration and high myopia define the syndrome; occipital encephalocele is a characteristic diagnostic feature.
Inherited biochemical or organelle metabolic defects; no additional damaged organ is shared by most patients across this broad umbrella.
Malignant tumour of vascular endothelial origin; childhood presentation does not establish another common organ site.
Inherited retinal dystrophy caused by biallelic ATF6 variants.
Cardiac electrical disorder with prolonged QT and ventricular arrhythmias.
Pathological TDP-43 inclusions damage neurons and glia in brain and spinal cord; protein aggregation alone does not imply an endocrine disorder.
Perivascular epithelioid-cell neoplasm arising in the lung; perivascular differentiation does not establish vascular disease.
Anaemia defined by small, hypochromic circulating red blood cells.
Respiratory ciliary dysfunction with bronchiectasis; recurrent middle-ear disease in 1/1 reported patient supports otologic involvement, with limited sample size.
Malignant notochordal tumour arising in the axial skeleton; neural compression varies by site and is not universal.
Oxidative phosphorylation defect with defining brain and liver dysfunction; amyotrophy 8/8 supports muscle involvement. Anaemia 4/4 and arthritis 3/9 omitted by cap.
Persistent mucosal keratotic plaque, predominantly oral in clinical practice; genital subtypes have no axis, and malignant transformation is a later risk.
Hair-shaft disorder with brittle beaded hair, alopecia and follicular hyperkeratosis.
Defining rhizomelic skeletal dysplasia, microcephaly and developmental delay; individual eye and cardiac abnormalities occur in only 1/4.
Hypotonia, ataxia and abnormal auditory brainstem responses define neurological dysfunction; nystagmus alone does not establish intrinsic eye damage or hearing loss.
Postinfectious chronic syndrome following SARS-CoV-2 infection; variable respiratory, cognitive and autonomic symptoms do not establish common direct organ damage.
Explicitly defined as disease affecting the brain.
Plasma-cell neoplasm with defining osteosclerotic bone lesions; peripheral neuropathy affects a majority in typical series. POEMS endocrine findings are not assumed universally.
Neoplasm located in the retina; retinal neural lineage does not add a separate neurological axis.
Most major forms involve testicular endocrine development, androgen synthesis or androgen action; additional organ defects are subtype-specific.
Congenital pulmonary venous drainage defect; pulmonary veins belong to the cardiovascular axis. Alveolar dysplasia is subtype-specific.
Inherited hypocalcified dental enamel defect; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Congenital facial nerve palsy with syndrome-defining variable hearing loss; impaired eyelid closure in 3/3 supports ocular involvement. Feeding symptoms add no GI damage.
GABRB1-related developmental and epileptic encephalopathy; cerebral visual impairment reflects brain dysfunction rather than intrinsic ocular disease.
